title: Days, months & time
listenFocus: A slow dialogue about the day and the time
practiceFocus: Say the greeting, the day, the date, and the time

points.title: One o’clock is singular
points.rule: Es means “it is” for the day and for one o’clock: es la una. Every other hour is son las. Y media is half past, and menos cuarto is a quarter to. On the clock, say de la tarde. For a plan, say por la tarde. Days and months are not capitalised. Day 3 uses this same es for people.

examples.spanish: Son las siete de la tarde.
examples.english: It is seven in the evening.

grammar.notYet: Estar (estoy, está, estamos). Minutes other than y media and menos cuarto. People with es come on day 3.

phrases.note: Days are not capitalised: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo.
Mañana means tomorrow. Por la mañana means in the morning.

phrases.english: What month is it? It is September.
phrases.note: Months are not capitalised: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre.
One o’clock uses una, not uno. The other hours: dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez, once, doce.

phrases.english: It is a quarter to ten.

phrases.note: Plans use por la tarde. The clock uses de la tarde: son las siete de la tarde.

phrases.spanish: Hoy es el doce de septiembre.
phrases.english: Today is the twelfth of September.
phrases.note: The date is el + number + de + month. Doce is twelve, from the clock numbers.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.english: Good morning. What day is it today?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.spanish: Son las siete de la tarde.
lines.english: It is seven in the evening.

practice.title: Time and date
practice.instruction: Greet for this part of the day, then say today’s day, the date, and the time. Add one plan for the weekend.
starters: Buenos días. / Buenas tardes. / Buenas noches.
tips: One o’clock is es la una. Every other hour is son las.
Days and months are not capitalised.
